songs.name: Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy early ’71 set with standout Tennessee Jed and Jack Straw
ai_show_review.blurb: The Atlanta show captures a fast‑moving snapshot of the 1971 Dead, highlighted by crisp renditions of Tennessee Jed, Jack Straw and Me And My Uncle. Recording quality is uneven – digi‑garble and dropouts interrupt the flow, though cleaned‑up sections sound surprisingly clear.
ai_show_review.review:
On November 11, 1971 at the Atlanta Municipal Auditorium the Dead delivered a brisk, high‑octane performance that feels more like a punchy highlight reel than an extended jam marathon. Set 1 rockets off with tight versions of Bertha and Playing In The Band before Jerry’s lead cuts sharp on Tennessee Jed and Jack Straw, while Bob’s vocal banter adds a playful edge to Me And My Uncle. The second set leans into the band’s early‑’70 feel‑good groove, moving through Mexicali Blues, One More Saturday Night and a spirited Not Fade Away → Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad → Not Fade Away medley that rolls straight into a rock‑n‑roll encore of Johnny B. Goode.

The soundboard source (gd71-11-11.sbd.yubah-dodd…) offers moments of crystal‑clear clarity, especially on the vocal harmonies and Phil’s warm bass lines, but is marred by digital garbling, occasional muddiness around Keith Godchaux’s keyboards, and a few dropouts that cut into Truckin'. The FM broadcast (gd1971-11-11.155920.FM.Flegel.flac16) provides a cleaner overall picture, making it the preferred listen for most fans. Despite its technical flaws, this show remains a worthwhile glimpse of the band’s tight early‑’71 chemistry.

best_recording.reason: FM broadcast avoids the digital garble of the soundboard and delivers a more consistent listening experience.

key_highlights: Fast, snappy set that captures the band’s early‑71 tightness.
Standout performances of Tennessee Jed, Jack Straw and Me And My Uncle.
Keith Godchaux’s early keyboard work adds texture despite odd mix balance.
Recording suffers from digi‑garble and dropouts, but cleaned sections are clear.

band_performance.Jerry: Fast, solid guitar work throughout; his tone cuts through the mix on Tennessee Jed and Jack Straw, with reliable background vocals on Me And My Uncle.
band_performance.Phil: Warm bass tones remain clear even when tape artifacts appear; anchors the high‑energy set with steady drive.
band_performance.Bob: Delivers confident lead vocals on Me And My Uncle and adds humorous stage banter that enhances the show’s lively vibe.
band_performance.Keith: Early keyboard contributions provide atmospheric color, though the mix around his playing is uneven in the soundboard source.
band_performance.Billy: Provides a steady rhythmic foundation; drumming stays tight despite occasional recording glitches.
